name: frotz
title: Frotz 2.54 (dfrotz, the dumb interface): the Z-machine that plays Infocom's Zork
fetch:
mkdir -p corpus/frotz && curl -Lo corpus/frotz/frotz-2.54.tar.gz https://gitlab.com/DavidGriffith/frotz/-/archive/2.54/frotz-2.54.tar.gz && tar -xzf corpus/frotz/frotz-2.54.tar.gz -C corpus/frotz && mkdir -p corpus/frotz/frotz-generated && printf '#define VERSION "2.54"
#define RELEASE_NOTES "Official release."
#define GIT_HASH "5a86de2f0799bde12699a0189ea12be8c96194a5"
#define GIT_HASH_SHORT "5a86de2"
#define GIT_DATE "2022-04-13 23:47:41 -0700"
' > corpus/frotz/frotz-generated/hash.h && printf '#ifndef COMMON_DEFINES_H
#define COMMON_DEFINES_H
#define RELEASE_NOTES "Official release."
#define UNIX
#define MAX_UNDO_SLOTS 500
#define MAX_FILE_NAME 80
#define TEXT_BUFFER_SIZE 512
#define INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE 200
#define STACK_SIZE 1024
#define USE_UTF8
#endif /* COMMON_DEFINES_H */
' > corpus/frotz/frotz-generated/defs.h
_doc: Frotz interprets Infocom's story files; Zork I-III are the originals from historicalsource (MIT), each with a COMPILED/zorkN.z3. The dumb interface is plain stdio -- a prompt, a line read, text written -- which makes a scripted game an exact oracle: the same commands must print the same transcript as a native dfrotz.
_units: The Makefile's `dumb` target: src/common's SOURCES, src/dumb's and src/blorb's (Blorb support is on by default).
_include: frotz.h includes "defs.h" and "hash.h", which the Makefile GENERATES into src/common. ../frotz-generated holds them as it writes them on Linux: hash.h from the release's own hash, defs.h with UNIX and USE_UTF8 and the default sizes.
_oracle: Zork I-III (historicalsource/zorkN, MIT: COMPILED/zorkN.z3) played from a command script, `--stdin=<script> --args='-m -p -q -s 1234 -w 80 zork1.z3'`, against a native dfrotz: the same text and byte-identical Quetzal saves. Compare the text with blank lines folded: dfrotz places them from screen cells whose colours make_cell (src/dumb/doutput.c) leaves uninitialised -- dinit.c:216's `== FORMAT_UNKNOWN || FORMAT_DISABLED` resets every -f to normal, so the branch that would set them never runs.
